title: Modular Monolith: A Primer
summary: Defines Modular Monolith as a single-deployment-unit system designed with modular principles including loose coupling, vertical slices, and well-defined module interfaces; argues modularity is orthogonal to monolithic architecture and refutes the misconception that monoliths cannot be well-designed.
when-to-read: Read this article when designing a system architecture and questioning whether a monolithic deployment model can support high-quality, modular design. If instead you are trying to decide between monolithic and microservice architectures based on their trade-offs, consult the decision-making tag or articles comparing architecture options.
